title: BFD session flap caused gRPC stream resets to control plane during rolling upgrade — follow-up
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
During a scheduled rolling upgrade of the Private control plane (2026.03), we observed a spike in gRPC stream resets from agents to the control plane in two regions. The root cause was short-lived BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) session flaps between two edge routers in the customer VPC path that caused transient route churn and asymmetric forwarding. The control plane's gRPC clients interpret the connection resets as permanent failures and tear down active sessions, triggering reconnect storms and temporary control plane CPU pressure.

Impact:
- Affected deployments: Private control planes in two customer regions (customer-facing private nodes).
- Observable symptoms: increased agent reconnects, higher 5xx rates on control-plane gRPC endpoints, longer scheduling latencies for Private jobs.
- Customer impact: intermittent request failures and delayed inference for ~18 minutes during the peak. High customer-impact classification due to production requests failing for a subset of Private customers.

Detection & Timeline (high-level):
- 2026-02-27 02:10 UTC: Canary rolling upgrade started (controlplane-2026.03).
- 2026-02-27 02:23 UTC: Grafana alert triggered: controlplane gRPC error rate > 5% (alert cp-grpc-err-high).
- 2026-02-27 02:27 UTC: SRE paged, preliminary mitigation: paused rollout in affected region.
- 2026-02-27 02:35 UTC: Network telemetry shows BGP/BFD state changes on customer-edge routers; router vendor logs indicate BFD session flaps.
- 2026-02-27 02:40 UTC: Manual rollback of one control-plane pod group reduced symptom frequency; full stability by 02:48 UTC.

Root Cause Analysis (summary):
Primary cause: BFD session flaps on the customer side introduced route convergence events across the path, creating asymmetric forwarding and packet reorder that led to TCP retransmits and gRPC stream resets.
Contributing factors at Redwood:
1) Control plane gRPC client aggressively resets connections on repeated stream failures rather than pausing/backing off at the connection layer.
2) Rolling upgrade reduced redundancy in control plane node groups briefly, making the system more sensitive to transient network disruptions.
3) We lacked a targeted runbook step for BFD-induced route churn detection — existing network runbooks focus on conntrack/NAT exhaustion and MTU issues.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Paused the rolling upgrade immediately in affected regions (SRE).
- Rolled back the newly upgraded node group to restore quorum redundancy and reduce reconnect storm impact (Infra Owner: Miguel Ortega).
- Temporarily increased gRPC server-side connection timeouts and enabled conservative keepalives to reduce premature resets (Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/4862).

Longer-term action plan (this ticket):
- Action A: Implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter for gRPC stream failures so transient network events do not cause immediate connection teardown. Owner: Connor Lee. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- Action B: Add a rollout policy flag to avoid reducing redundancy below N during rolling upgrades in Private deployments; default to conservative step sizes when BFD/BGP churn is detected. Owner: Release Engineering. ETA: 2026-04-05.
- Action C: Add network telemetry alerting for BFD/BGP flaps correlated with control-plane gRPC error spikes and automate a pause in rollouts when detected. Owner: Network Observability (SRE). ETA: 2026-03-30.
- Action D: Update Private runbooks to include BFD/BGP diagnostics and recommended remediation steps for customer network partners. Owner: Solutions Eng (Priya Patel). ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Action E: Post-incident run of a chaos test simulating asymmetric forwarding during a rolling upgrade in our staging VPC to validate mitigations. Owner: Reliability Team. ETA: 2026-04-01.

Trade-offs discussed: 
- Increasing gRPC timeouts reduces sensitivity to real failures and can delay detection of genuine control-plane issues. We will scope changes to connection-level backoff and keep per-RPC deadlines to preserve correctness while avoiding full connection teardown.
- Adding automated rollout pauses improves safety but increases rollout duration; we intend to gate this behind a customer-tier policy and make it opt-out for low-risk upgrades.

Postmortem owners & reviewers:
- Incident lead: Aisha Khan
- RCA owner / assignee for follow-ups: Connor Lee
- Network observability reviewer: Miguel Ortega
- Solutions engineering reviewer: Priya Patel

Status & next steps:
- Patch PR to increase gRPC keepalive/timeouts merged as emergency short-term mitigation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/4862 (merged 2026-02-27).
- Branch opened for client backoff changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/4890 (WIP).
- Runbook draft updated and posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/BFD-BGP-Runbook (internal).
- This ticket tracks implementation of Actions A, B, and C and coordination with customer-facing teams for D.

Notes:
- No customer data was exposed; this is strictly a connectivity/regional availability incident.
- We should coordinate with affected customers' network teams to confirm BFD timers that caused sensitivity; SRE will open follow-up customer-facing dockets where needed.
